records.statement_text: A Town Council special meeting was convened on October 9, 2024 at approximately 7:01 p.m.
Per the annexation report summary, the Town of Alpine's mill levy is 5 mills.
The Town of Alpine water system was shut down on May 21, 2026 due to a water main break.
The Town Council scheduled a Budget Work Session for Thursday, June 11, 2026 at 2:00 PM.
Bacteriological testing confirmed the water met all safe drinking-water standards before the advisory was lifted.
The council reported it took no action during its executive session before reconvening the regular session.

The Alpine Planning and Zoning Board passed a resolution calling for an emergency temporary moratorium on annexation petitions and building permits in certain zoning categories within the municipal boundaries.
The Alpine Planning and Zoning commission brought forth Resolution Number 2024-033 to implement a six-month building and annexation moratorium, excluding single family residences.
A capacity study of Alpine water and sewer systems was requested and conducted by the town engineer.
If all annexed properties with will-serve letters were fully built out, the Alpine sewer system would reach 92 percent of maximum day capacity.
The Alpine mega well has a large capacity rated at approximately 2,500 gallons in an 8-hour test with minimal drawdown, and can produce approximately 1,500 gallons per minute.
The Town of Alpine operates at a five-mill property tax levy and cannot increase property taxes unless the fire district arrangement changes.
The town submitted intended use plans to the state drinking water revolving fund for water infrastructure improvements.
The Alpine Planning and Zoning Board discussed the dark sky initiative at a meeting.
The Alpine fire district is funded through a mill levy assessed on property taxes.
The third and final capital budget meeting for the Town of Alpine was scheduled for Thursday at 3:00 PM.
Based on Alpine's 5 percent combined sales tax rate, projected alcohol sales from a liquor license would generate approximately 32,800 to 41,000 dollars per year in additional sales tax revenue.
Resolution 2026-010 authorized the Town of Alpine to be represented at meetings of the Alpine Meadows Property Owner Association.
Town staff recommended the Alpine Town Council adopt an ordinance to standardize public notice requirements across all town processes including subdivisions and annexations.

The second reading of the Alpine budget included capital projects and showed overall revenues and funding sources increasing by approximately 690,000 dollars across general, water, and wastewater funds.
A motion was made to approve the annexation agreement for the Alpine Lakes Addition involving property owners and approximately 61 acres contiguous to the Town of Alpine.
Ordinance 2025-00001 of the Town of Alpine prohibits extending water and sewer services to property outside the incorporated town boundaries.
The Town Council voted on Resolution 2026-027 certifying the Dry Dog Development LLC Alpine Apex Annexation Petition.
A motion was made to approve a 12-month extension for the Alpine Flats building permits for buildings three and four beyond the June 12, 2027 expiration date.
The clerk confirmed a quorum of the Alpine Town Council with all members present.
The Alpine Town Council adopted the meeting agenda unanimously.

The proposed moratorium covered building permits in areas zoned multi-unit residential (R2), mixed residential and commercial (MRC), commercial (C), light industrial (LI), public and community services (PCF), and recreation and conservation (RC) within the municipal boundaries of the Town of Alpine, Wyoming.
During the proposed moratorium, the Town of Alpine would continue to accept, review, and process applications for residential buildings within all other zones.
A motion was made to approve resolution number 2026-005 amending resolution number 2026-001 regarding official appointments for the Town of Alpine.
A motion was made to approve resolution number 2026-006 acknowledging the award of $25,000 from the America 250 grant program.
The Alpine Town Council unanimously approved the consent agenda.
A motion was made to approve resolution number 2026-007, a resolution waiving subdivision fees and associated mailing requirements.
A motion was made to approve resolution number 2026-008 authorizing the submission of a federal mineral royalty capital construction account application.
A motion was made to approve resolution number 2026-009 for the submission of a federal mineral royalty capital construction account.
A motion was made to approve the first reading of ordinance number 2026-001 creating the position of town administrator.
A motion was made to approve resolution number 2026-010 authorizing representation of the Town of Alpine at meetings of the Alpine Meadows.
For the upcoming application period and fiscal year 2026-27, the Town of Alpine will emphasize projects with extended timelines.
The Alpine Town Council considered ordinance number 2026-00008.
An ordinance carried on first reading at the Alpine Town Council.
The mayor's report at the Alpine Town Council meeting focused on upcoming Fourth of July preparations.
The Alpine Lakes Addition annexation agreement passed the Town Council by a 4-to-1 vote.
The Alpine Town Council considered resolution number 2026-027.
Dry Dog Development LLC held a pre-petition meeting with town staff and completed their petition application for annexation.
The Alpine Town Clerk reported that existing ordinances regulating recreational fires and fireworks contradict each other regarding permitted fireworks dates in the Town of Alpine.
The Alpine Town Council held a discussion regarding a draft ordinance establishing administrative fees and cost recovery for town services.
The Alpine Town Council approved ordinance number 2026-001 on third reading, carrying the ordinance that creates the position of town administrator.
The Planning and Zoning Board approved a new single family residence application R26-0000006.
The Planning and Zoning Board approved building permit application RB26-00009.
The Tourism Board approved a reconciliation of a grant to Alpine Trails and Pathways in the amount of $8,000 for grooming cross-country ski trails.
The Alpine Town Council considered the second reading of ordinance 2026-008, an interim permitting update.
The Alpine Town Council considered the second reading of ordinance number 2026-0055 establishing fees for administrative services, return payments, and staff reimbursements.
The Alpine Town Council considered the second reading of ordinance number 2026-010 for the Dead Horse Planned Unit Development.
The Alpine Town Council considered resolution number 2026-022 certifying the Boardlock 2 Lot 18 annexation petition.
The Alpine Town Council considered resolution number 2026-019 adopting and accepting the mill levy tax base of 5 mills for the fiscal year 2027.
The Alpine Town Council convened a budget work session on May 7th, 2026.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $4,840 in funding to Trout Unlimited.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $8,000 in funding for the Winter Jubilee event.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $2,500 to the Town of Alpine for trash receptacles on behalf of the Impacts of Tourism program.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $17,000 for the Alpine Fire District for impacts of tourism.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $5,000 to the Town of Alpine for winter bridge trail management.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $30,000 to the Town of Alpine for the lease of a snow groomer.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $25,000 in funding for the Reggae and the Rockies event.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $15,000 to the Town of Alpine for Fourth of July fireworks.
The Alpine Tourism Board approved $3,000 for Alpine Mountain Days to the Town of Alpine.
The Planning and Zoning Board approved a single family residence building permit application RB2600000011.
The Alpine Planning and Zoning Commission discussed reviewing the PUD process and LUDC to identify operational deficiencies and recommend updates for better alignment with industry standards.
During the P&Z discussion, it was noted that the master plan is a guiding document, while the land use and development code is the core regulatory instrument that needs substantive changes.
The Planning and Zoning Commission identified a gap in the development review process, noting the need for an intermediate review mechanism between a basic annexation report and a full PUD.
The Design Review Committee reviewed a building design approaching 10,000 square feet, noting that the designers broke up the massing to fit the Alpine entry context.
The proposed building at the Alpine Design Review is associated with Kitty Academy, which requires fencing for its play area.
Alpine Lakes Commercial Center, LLC submitted an application for annexation into the Town of Alpine for a property legally described as Lot 1 of the Alpine Lakes Subdivision.
The Alpine Planning and Zoning Commission scheduled a public hearing to review the Planned Unit Development application for the Alpine Lakes Commercial Center annexation.
The Town of Alpine Town Council rescheduled its regularly scheduled June 16, 2026 meeting.
Casa Mezcal, LLC filed an application with the Town of Alpine for a Restaurant Liquor License.
The Alpine Master Plan establishes a twenty-year direction for the Town of Alpine's growth, evolution, and preservation of its mountain character.
The Alpine Master Plan identifies transforming downtown Alpine into a memorable and active main street as a key land use goal.
The Alpine Master Plan includes a goal to incentivize thoughtful and sustainable growth that reflects the character of Alpine.
The Alpine Master Plan's economic vitality goal is to build on Alpine's strategic location to capture economic opportunities from regional traffic and tourism.
The Alpine Master Plan includes a housing goal to provide housing options that support Alpine's evolving role in the region.
The Alpine Master Plan establishes a goal to protect and conserve the natural environment that makes Alpine special.
The Alpine Master Plan includes a goal to ensure reliable town services for current and future residents' health, safety, education, and quality of life.
The Alpine Master Plan includes a goal to preserve and enhance the region's world class recreation and open space.
The Town of Alpine issued a notice about upcoming bridge maintenance work on the US Highway 89 bridge, scheduled by the Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT).
WYDOT and contractor Reiman Corporation will perform an epoxy overlay application on the US Highway 89 bridge deck at approximately mile marker 118, beginning June 4, 2026.
